newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Arthuis rejects call for Ffr depreciation.
newsitem.headline: France's Arthuis rejects call for Ffr depreciation.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis rejected on Thursday calls by former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing for a sharp depreciation of the franc, saying it would only exacerbate the country's economic troubles.
"We know very well that when the franc depreciates, interest rates are pushed higher by the market," Arthuis told the Senate.

"If we choose that route, it will endanger growth and jobs. The best (currency) parities are those which give us the lowest interest rates," he said, repeating comments made earlier to afternoon daily Le Monde.
"There is no question of changing the pivot rates in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), in particular between the franc and the mark," he said.
Arthuis said the government's strong franc policy had delivered "unprecedented" low interest rates and called it "an illusion that unlocking the franc from the mark would solve all our problems."
Giscard d'Estaing, writing in the weekly magazine L'Express on Wednesdsay, said a lower franc was needed to breathe life into France's flagging economy.
